_comment: B1.b two-head duration (design doc §三 3.1b, pre-registered 2026-09-08, user decision). B1_point_matched dissociated the two B1 gains: the PATH gain is the duration weight (point head, final_time_loss_weight 26 -> ADE 1248 vs native32 1322, chamfer 177 vs 224) and the ARRIVAL-TIME gain is the quantile head (MAE 23.9 vs 25.9 s pooled, 10.3 vs 13.6 s straight-in) — and they do not overlap. In B1_quantile the rollout duration IS the quantile head's q50, so the head's path cost is forced onto the trajectory. duration_head=two-head decouples them: a point head (weight final_time_loss_weight) drives the rollout duration; a quantile head (pinball, weight duration_quantile_loss_weight) only emits the ETA distribution that B2 calibrates and B3 decodes. One arm, same base as B1 (N=32 native supervision, no latent). PRE-REGISTERED GATES: (1) pooled ADE within seed noise (30 m) of B1_point_matched's 1248 m AND pooled duration MAE within 1 s of B1_quantile's 23.9 s (straight-in within 1 s of 10.3 s) — both at once, on the point head's duration for ADE and the quantile head's q50 for MAE; (2) the five-cut DEPLOYED coverage (run_ts_eta_calibration --half-seed probes, --readout-only) inside the gate-2 bands; (3) gate 3.4-3 fan geometry as for B3 (predict --cta-from-quantiles on the quantile head). VETO: either metric worse than its single-head donor beyond noise (ADE > 1278 or MAE > 24.9 s) — then the heads interfere and the deliverable stays two models. Single seed; a second seed of B1_point_matched (B1_point_matched_s2024) is queued separately to confirm the 74 m before the main recipe adopts the weight.

arms.label: point head (duration weight 26) drives the rollout, quantile head (pinball weight 1) emits the ETA distribution
